Tell me in about 200 words why people in India are switching to UPI, with a short list of 3 reasons
7:16 AM

People in India are switching to UPI because it makes paying as easy as sending a message: instant, free for most everyday payments, and accepted almost everywhere. You scan a code or type a phone number or UPI ID, confirm with your PIN, and the money moves from bank to bank in seconds. No card machine, no cash, no waiting for change.

It also spread fast because nearly everyone could join in. Small shops, tea stalls and street vendors need only a printed QR code, not special equipment. Once the local vendor accepted it, customers had little reason to carry cash. Apps like PhonePe, Google Pay and Paytm, along with bank apps, all work on the same network, so you aren't tied to one.

The three main reasons:

Speed and simplicity: A payment takes seconds and needs just a scan and a PIN.
Low or no cost: Most people and small shops pay nothing to send or receive, which beats card fees and handling cash.
Works everywhere: Any bank account, any app, from a big mall to a roadside stall.

Safety helps too. You never share your card or bank details, and every payment needs your PIN. Put together, that makes UPI the easy default for daily spending.
